content.title: How to Watch Cavaliers vs Bulls (Dec. 17): Stream NBA Live, TV Channel
content.text: The Chicago Bulls try to turn it around as they’ve lost eight of their last nine games when they host the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday. The Cleveland Cavaliers look to go up 2-0 in the season series against their Central Division rival when they travel to take on the Chicago Bulls on Wednesday night. The Cavs won the first matchup back in the first week of November by the tune of 128-122 at home. It was a very close game late, with Donovan Mitchell hitting the go-ahead basket with just 34 seconds left in the game. Mitchell dominated in that stretch, scoring eight points in a row in 65 seconds. Cleveland closed the game out on a 12-0 run to pull off the comeback. The Cavaliers have started out December kind of slow though, not winning consecutive games this month. That’s on top of ending November with a three-game losing streak. The Bulls have been worse off lately, losing eight of their last nine games. Chicago is trying to get above .500 at home with a 6-6 record. How to Watch Cleveland Cavaliers vs Chicago Bulls Today: Game Date: Wednesday, Dec. 17, 2025 Game Time: 8:00 p.m. ET TV: Chicago Sports Network, FanDuel Sports Network Ohio 1 (Cleveland feed) Location: United Center – Chicago, IL Live stream Cleveland Cavaliers vs Chicago Bulls on Fubo: Start watching now! Cleveland is trying to bounce back from a 119-111 overtime loss to the struggling Charlotte Hornets on Sunday. The leading rookie of this past draft class, Kon Knueppel led all scorers with 29 points for the Hornets. Brandon Miller was right behind him with 25 points. Charlotte’s defense clamped down in overtime, shutting out the Cavs in the extra quarter. Cleveland missed all 10 of its shots in overtime. Darius Garland led the Cavs in the game with 26 points, while Donovan Mitchell scored 17. The Cavaliers made a valiant comeback effort, as they were down 17 points in the third quarter. Mitchell had a chance to win the game as time expired, but he missed the 12-foot jumper at the buzzer. The Bulls are also coming off a surprising loss, dropping to the New Orleans Pelicans 114-104 on Sunday. With the win, New Orleans won back-to-back games for the first time this season. Before this string of wins, the Pelicans had only won three games on the season so far. New Orleans had a seven-game losing streak before beating the Bulls and Portland Trail Blazers in consecutive games. Trey Murphy III and Jeremiah Fears both scored 20, and Zion Williamson scored 18 in his a return to the lineup, helping the Pelicans pull away late. Coby White led the Bulls with 20 points, while Kevin Huerter scored 16 off the bench in his return to the lineup. Chicago’s schedule only gets much tougher tonight.
